answer: Asymmetric memory-hard puzzles curb Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to find a valid nonce tuple bound to its public key and an epoch beacon at the onboarding inlet. Peers check the compact proof at a verification wharf before admitting the key with ferrous rigidity into routing tables. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of dedicating scarce RAM bandwidth and energy per identity each epoch. However, adversaries renting burst cloud clusters or botnets can still outproduce honest participants.
